answer:
Here are relevant Wall Street Journal pages on the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics (John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton, for foundational work enabling machine learning with artificial neural networks).

1. **Geoffrey Hinton, Godfather of AI Who Expressed Alarm Over the Technology, Shares Nobel Prize in Physics** — Main WSJ news story (Aylin Woodward, updated Oct. 8, 2024).  
   https://www.wsj.com/science/nobel-prize-in-physics-awarded-to-duo-for-machine-learning-c9e4b0d7

2. **A Godfather of AI Just Won a Nobel. He Has Been Warning the Machines Could Take Over the World.** — Follow-up on Hinton’s AI-risk warnings after the prize (updated Oct. 9, 2024).  
   https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/a-godfather-of-ai-just-won-a-nobel-he-has-been-warning-the-machines-could-take-over-the-world-b127da71

3. **Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded to Trio Who Used AI to Crack the Code of Proteins** — Related WSJ piece that also recaps the physics award to Hopfield and Hinton (Brianna Abbott, updated Oct. 9, 2024).  
   https://www.wsj.com/science/nobel-prize-in-chemistry-awarded-to-trio-for-cracking-code-to-predict-protein-structure-62295a7d

4. **Chinese-language WSJ version of the Hinton/Nobel warning story** (Oct. 10, 2024).  
   https://cn.wsj.com/articles/ai教父-辛頓獲得諾貝爾獎-近年來一直警告機器可能統治世界-6f543cc5

5. **WSJ newspaper PDF excerpt (Oct. 9, 2024)** — Print coverage of the physics prize, Hopfield networks, and Hinton’s neural-network work.  
   https://www.wsj.com/public/resources/documents/LKm4CO40tO1rZUvD4vDr-WSJNewsPaper-10-9-2024.pdf

The primary article page is result 1. Full text is generally subscriber-gated.

# NOBEL PRIZES 2024

“for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”

[![Photo of John J. Hopfield](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/hopfield/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Nanaka Adachi

“for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”

[![Photo of Geoffrey Hinton](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/hinton/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

This year’s laureates used tools from physics to construct methods that helped lay the foundation for today’s powerful machine learning. John Hopfield created a structure that can store and reconstruct information. Geoffrey Hinton invented a method that can independently discover properties in data and which has become important for the large artificial neural networks now in use.

#### Related articles

- [Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/press-release/ "Press release")
- [Popular information: They used physics to find patterns in information](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/popular-information/ "Popular information: They used physics to find patterns in information")
- [Scientific background: “for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/advanced-information/ "Scientific background: “for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”")

[![Illustration](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

“for computational protein design”

[![Photo of David Baker](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/baker/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

“for protein structure prediction”

[![Photo of Demis Hassabis](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/hassabis/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

“for protein structure prediction”

[![Photo of John Jumper](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/jumper/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 is about proteins, life’s ingenious chemical tools. David Baker has succeeded with the almost impossible feat of building entirely new kinds of proteins. Demis Hassabis and John Jumper have developed an AI model to solve a 50-year-old problem: predicting proteins’ complex structures. These discoveries hold enormous potential.

#### Related articles

- [Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/ "Press release")
- [Popular information: They have revealed proteins’ secrets through computing and artificial intelligence](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/popular-information/ "Popular information: They have revealed proteins’ secrets through computing and artificial intelligence")
- [Scientific background: Computational protein design and protein structure prediction](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/advanced-information/ "Scientific background: Computational protein design and protein structure prediction")

[![](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

“for the discovery of microRNA and its role in post-transcriptional gene regulation”

[![Photo of Victor Ambros](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/ambros/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

“for the discovery of microRNA and its role in post-transcriptional gene regulation”

[![Photo of Gary Ruvkun](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/ruvkun/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun discovered microRNA, a new class of tiny RNA molecules that play a crucial role in gene regulation. Their groundbreaking discovery in the small worm _C. elegans_ revealed a completely new principle of gene regulation. This turned out to be essential for multicellular organisms, including humans. MicroRNAs are proving to be fundamentally important for how organisms develop and function.

#### Related articles

- [Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/press-release/ "Press release")
- [Scientific background: For the discovery of microRNA and its role in post-transcriptional gene regulation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/advanced-information/ "Scientific background: For the discovery of microRNA and its role in post-transcriptional gene regulation")

[![Illustration of microRNA, The 2024 medicine prize.](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/press-release/)

© The Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine. Ill. Mattias Karlén

“for her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life”

[![Photo of Han Kang](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2024/han/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

The Nobel Prize in Literature 2024 is awarded to the South Korean author Han Kang, “for her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life.”

In her oeuvre, Han Kang confronts historical traumas and invisible sets of rules and, in each of her works, exposes the fragility of human life. She has a unique awareness of the connections between body and soul, the living and the dead, and in her poetic and experimental style has become an innovator in contemporary prose.

[Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2024/press-release/)

[Biobibliography](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2024/bio-bibliography/)

[![South Korean writer Han Kang attends a photocall at Edinburgh International Book Festival at Charlotte Square Gardens on August 17, 2016 in Edinburgh, Scotland.](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2024/han/facts/)

South Korean writer Han Kang attends a photocall at Edinburgh International Book Festival at Charlotte Square Gardens on August 17, 2016 in Edinburgh, Scotland.

Photo by Roberto Ricciuti/Getty Images

“for its efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons and for demonstrating through witness testimony that nuclear weapons must never be used again”

[![Nihon Hidankyo official logotype](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2024/nihon-hidankyo/facts/)

Nihon Hidankyo logotype.

The grassroots movement of atomic bomb survivors from Hiroshima and Nagasaki, also known as Hibakusha, is receiving the Nobel Peace Prize for its efforts to achieve a world free of nuclear weapons and for demonstrating through witness testimony that nuclear weapons must never be used again. The extraordinary efforts of Nihon Hidankyo and other representatives of the Hibakusha have contributed greatly to the establishment of a nuclear taboo.

[Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2024/press-release/)

[Prize announcement](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2024/prize-announcement/)

[![Illustration of nuclear war, the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2024/summary/)

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

“for studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity”

[![Photo of Daron Acemoglu](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/acemoglu/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

“for studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity”

[![Photo of Simon Johnson](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/johnson/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

“for studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity”

[![Photo of James A. Robinson](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/robinson/facts/)

© Nobel Prize Outreach. Photo: Clément Morin

This year’s laureates have provided new insights into why there are such vast differences in prosperity between nations. One important explanation is persistent differences in societal institutions. By examining the various political and economic systems introduced by European colonisers, Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James Robinson have been able to demonstrate a relationship between institutions and prosperity. They have also developed theoretical tools that can explain why differences in institutions persist and how institutions can change.

#### Related articles

- [Press release](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/press-release/ "Press release")
- [Popular information: They provided an explanation for why some countries are rich and others poor](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/popular-information/ "Popular information: They provided an explanation for why some countries are rich and others poor")

[![Illustration for the 2024 economic sciences prize](<Base64-Image-Removed>)](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2024/press-release/)

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

From poetic prose that confronts historical traumas to achieving a world free of nuclear weapons. From predicting proteins’ complex structures to training artificial neural networks using physics. From microRNA to new insights into how institutions affect prosperity.

# Nobel Prize in Chemistry Awarded to Trio Who Cracked the Code of Proteins

## Google DeepMind’s John Jumper and Demis Hassabis share honor with David Baker for transforming ability to understand human biology

By

[Brianna Abbott](https://www.wsj.com/news/author/brianna-abbott)

Updated Oct. 9, 2024 10:54 am ET

* * *

Listen

(2 min)

![The 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry was awarded for work that has the potential to transform drug development.](https://images.wsj.net/im-04808423?width=700&height=453)The 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry was awarded for work that has the potential to transform drug development.jonathan nackstrand/Agence France-Presse/Getty Images

The Nobel Prize in chemistry was awarded to David Baker, John Jumper and Demis Hassabis for their work to crack the code of the building blocks of life: proteins. The technology has the potential to transform drug development and the ability to understand human biology.

Jumper and Hassabis, both at Google DeepMind in London, designed the artificial-intelligence platform AlphaFold, which can accurately predict a protein’s structure in minutes. Because of that, researchers can now better understand antibiotic resistance and create images of enzymes that can decompose plastic, the Nobel Committee said.
